title: How electric cars work
examples: How does the battery power the wheels?
What is the difference between charging and running?
Can the car use the brakes to make more power?

explain.say: Today we learn how electric cars move.

items: Electric Motor: Converts energy to motion

explain.say: The battery stores the electrical energy for the car.
The electric motor uses this power to spin the wheels.
Regenerative braking captures energy when you slow down.
Charging means connecting the car to an external power source.

items: Battery stores energy for next trip

explain.say: In real life, when you go down a hill, regen braking helps.

faq.q: Does the motor use electricity from the battery directly?
faq.a: Yes, the battery supplies electricity to the motor to make it turn. It is a continuous flow of power.
asks: Where does the power come from?
Is the battery the power source?

faq.q: What exactly happens during regenerative braking?
faq.a: It reverses the motor's job; instead of using power, it creates it by slowing down. This extra power goes back to the battery.
asks: How does braking help the battery?
Is regenerative braking like a brake pad?

faq.q: Is charging the same as running the car?
faq.a: No, running uses stored energy, while charging adds new energy from an outside source. Think of it like refilling a phone.
asks: Do I need to charge it before I drive?
What is the difference between charging and driving?

faq.q: How big is the battery usually in an electric car?
faq.a: The battery size determines how far the car can travel on one full charge. Larger batteries mean longer ranges.
asks: Does battery size matter for distance?

faq.q: Do electric cars still need brakes?
faq.a: Yes, they still need physical brakes for safety, but regenerative braking assists them greatly. They work together for stopping.
asks: Can I rely only on regen braking?
Are the brakes useless in an EV?

facts: Electric cars use a large battery pack to store energy.
The electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
Regenerative braking recovers energy when the car decelerates.
Charging connects the car to an external electrical grid source.

quiz.say: What component stores the energy needed to move the car?
quiz.why: The battery is designed specifically to hold electrical energy for later use.

wrong.0: The braking system slows the car down; it is not the main storage unit.
wrong.2: The motor uses the energy; it does not store it.
wrong.3: The wheels only move; they do not store electrical energy.

quiz.say: When slowing down, what process helps put energy back into the battery?
quiz.why: This process turns the motor into a generator, sending power back to the battery.

wrong.0: Charging requires an external source, not just slowing down.
wrong.2: Friction braking wastes energy as heat, it does not recover it.
wrong.3: Idling just uses small amounts of power; it does not recover energy.

quiz.say: If a car is connected to the wall socket at home, what action is happening?
quiz.why: Charging is the act of replenishing the stored energy from an external source.

wrong.0: Motorizing is the process of using the power, not adding it.
wrong.2: Driving uses the stored energy; it is the output action.
wrong.3: Regenerating only happens when the car is slowing down, not when plugged in.
